headline: A song that began as AI-made music has become an internet craze since two human singers re-recorded it.
score_reason: Lowered from 2: the song dates from May and has been viral for weeks, so today's piece is a look-back.
importance_line: It shows how unclear authorship has become when a person writes the words and a machine makes the sound, which matters to musicians and listeners, with the doubt that Mashable relies partly on Pitchfork and Know Your Meme.
summary: Mashable reports that "GG EZ", a gaming-slang pop-rap song first released in May by an anonymous Japanese producer who says they make music with AI, went viral in a version re-sung by creators Kaien Nuen and Angelina "Sugar" Zhang, with one seven-second clip passing 72 million views on X. Mashable says the case shows how hard it is to say who "made" a song when a person supplied the words and direction and a machine supplied the sound.
notes: Exact release day not stated (May 2026); remake late Aug 2026. Mashable cites Pitchfork, Forbes, Know Your Meme.
